# Configure custom domains

A custom domain lets you reach your HCP Vault Dedicated cluster at a hostname
you own, such as `vault.example.com`, instead of the default `*.hashicorp.cloud`
address. HCP issues and renews a TLS certificate that includes your custom
domain, so clients can connect over HTTPS without certificate warnings. Your
cluster stays reachable on its default HCP address while the custom domain is
enabled.

Custom domains support publicly and privately accessible AWS and Azure clusters
in all HCP Vault Dedicated tiers. You enable, update, and disable a custom
domain with the HCP API. Your DNS records stay in your own DNS provider. The
examples on this page use Amazon Route 53.

@include 'private-beta-feature.mdx'

## How it works

1. You create two CNAME records in the public DNS zone for your domain. The
   first routes traffic for your custom domain to your cluster. The second,
   `_acme-challenge`, lets HCP prove that you control the domain so it can
   issue a certificate from Let's Encrypt.
1. You send a `PATCH` request to the HCP API to enable the custom domain on
   your cluster.
1. HCP checks that both CNAME records exist and point to the right place, then
   creates the certificate. Certificate creation is asynchronous. The API
   returns an operation in the `PENDING` state and the operation takes about 10
   to 15 minutes to reach `DONE`.

## Prerequisites

- An HCP organization and project with an existing HCP Vault Dedicated cluster,
  and permission to update that cluster. You can only configure a custom domain
  on a cluster that already exists.
- Your HCP organization enrolled in the Custom Domains private beta. If it is
  not, the API returns `403`. Contact HashiCorp to request access.
- A domain you own, with a **public** DNS zone and permission to create and
  delete records in it. For Route 53, this is a public hosted zone.
- The [HCP CLI](/hcp/docs/cli/install) (`hcp`), `curl`, `jq`, `dig`, and
  `openssl` on macOS or Linux. On Windows, use WSL.

### Limitations

- You can configure one custom domain per cluster.
- After a successful change, you cannot change the custom domain again for 24
  hours. Refer to [Throttling](#throttling).
- HCP issues and manages the certificate. You cannot provide your own
  certificate.
- Wildcard domains, such as `*.example.com`, are not supported.
- Private-only DNS is not supported. The `_acme-challenge` CNAME record must be
  publicly resolvable, or certificate issuance fails. If you use split-horizon
  DNS, create the `_acme-challenge` record in your public zone and keep
  traffic routing in your private zone.
- You configure custom domains through the HCP API only. The HCP Portal does
  not support them yet.

<Note title="Subject to change">

Request fields, behavior, and limits can change before general availability.

</Note>

## Configure a custom domain

### Set environment variables

Collect the following values and export them in the terminal you use for the
rest of this page.

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID` | Your HCP organization ID. Run `hcp organizations list`. |
| `HCP_PROJECT_ID` | The ID of the project that contains your cluster. Run `hcp projects list`. |
| `HCP_VAULT_ID` | Your cluster ID, which is the cluster name. For example, `my-vault-cluster`. |
| `HCP_CLUSTER_DNS` | The host name of your cluster URL, without `https://` and without the port. For example, `my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud`. |
| `HCP_PROVIDER_NAME` | The cloud provider of your cluster, `aws` or `azure`. |
| `HCP_REGION_NAME` | The region of your cluster. For example, `us-west-2`. |
| `HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN` | The domain you want to use, in the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`. For example, `vault.example.com`. |

1. Sign in to HCP.

   ```shell-session
   $ hcp auth login
   ```

1. Export the variables.

   ```shell-session
   $ export HCP_API_ADDRESS="api.cloud.hashicorp.com" \
       HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID="<HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID>" \
       HCP_PROJECT_ID="<HCP_PROJECT_ID>" \
       HCP_VAULT_ID="<HCP_VAULT_ID>" \
       HCP_CLUSTER_DNS="<HCP_CLUSTER_DNS>" \
       HCP_PROVIDER_NAME="<aws-or-azure>" \
       HCP_REGION_NAME="<HCP_REGION_NAME>" \
       HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN="<subdomain>.<primary-domain>" \
       HCP_API_TOKEN="$(hcp auth print-access-token)"
   ```

   <Warning>

   The access token is a credential. Do not paste it into tickets, chat, or
   shared documents. It is short lived. If an API call returns `401`, run
   `hcp auth login` again and refresh `HCP_API_TOKEN`.

   </Warning>

### Create the CNAME records

Create the following two records in the public DNS zone for your primary domain
**before** you call the HCP API. If the records are missing or have not
propagated, the API call fails.

| | Record 1: custom domain | Record 2: ACME challenge |
|---|---|---|
| **Name** | `vault` | `_acme-challenge.vault` |
| **Type** | `CNAME` | `CNAME` |
| **Value** | Your cluster DNS name (`HCP_CLUSTER_DNS`) | `_acme-challenge.` followed by your cluster DNS name |
| **TTL** | `300` | `300` |

For the custom domain `vault.example.com`, the records look like this:

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```text
vault.example.com                   CNAME  my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud
_acme-challenge.vault.example.com   CNAME  _acme-challenge.my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

To create the records in Route 53:

1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open **Route 53**.

1. In the left navigation, select **Hosted zones**.

1. Select the hosted zone for your primary domain. Its type must be **Public**.

1. On the **Records** tab, select **Create record**.

1. Enter the values for Record 1. Set **Record type** to `CNAME`, **TTL** to
   `300`, and **Routing policy** to **Simple routing**.

1. Select **Add another record** and enter the values for Record 2.

1. Select **Create records**, then confirm both records appear on the
   **Records** tab with the values you entered.

### Verify DNS

DNS propagation can take a few minutes. Query both records from your own
network.

```shell-session
$ dig +short CNAME "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
$ dig +short CNAME "_acme-challenge.${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
```

Each command must print the matching HCP name, ending in a dot.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```text
my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud.
_acme-challenge.my-vault-cluster-public-vault-1a2b3c4d.5e6f7a8b.z1.hashicorp.cloud.
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

<Warning title="Wait for both records">

Do not call the HCP API until both commands return the expected value. If you
do, the request fails with `Failed to lookup CNAME record`.

</Warning>

### Enable the custom domain

Send a `PATCH` request to the cluster resource with `is_enabled` set to `true`.

```shell-session
$ curl --silent --show-error --request PATCH \
    "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" \
    --data @- <<EOF | jq
{
  "id": "${HCP_VAULT_ID}",
  "location": {
    "organization_id": "${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}",
    "project_id": "${HCP_PROJECT_ID}",
    "region": {
      "provider": "${HCP_PROVIDER_NAME}",
      "region": "${HCP_REGION_NAME}"
    }
  },
  "config": {
    "network_config": {
      "custom_domain_config": {
        "is_enabled": true,
        "custom_domain": "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
      }
    }
  }
}
EOF
```

A successful request returns HTTP `200` and an operation in the `PENDING`
state. `PENDING` means HCP accepted the request, not that the domain is live.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```json
{
  "operation": {
    "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
    "state": "PENDING",
    "location": {
      "organization_id": "<HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID>",
      "project_id": "<HCP_PROJECT_ID>",
      "region": {
        "provider": "aws",
        "region": "us-west-2"
      }
    },
    "link": {
      "type": "hashicorp.vault.cluster",
      "id": "my-vault-cluster"
    },
    "created_at": "2026-11-03T10:15:30.123456Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-11-03T10:15:30.123456Z",
    "visibility": "EXPOSED"
  }
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The sample omits some internal fields. If the request is rejected, refer to
[Errors](#errors).

### Track the operation

Optionally, track the operation until it finishes. Set the operation ID from the
`operation.id` field of the response, then read the operation state.

```shell-session
$ export HCP_OPERATION_ID="<operation.id>"
$ curl --silent --show-error \
    "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/operation/2020-05-05/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/operations/${HCP_OPERATION_ID}" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" | jq '.operation.state'
```

The state is `"PENDING"` while HCP works on the change. Repeat the call every
few minutes. The operation is finished when it prints `"DONE"`.

## Verify the configuration

After the operation reaches `DONE`, confirm the custom domain is active.

1. Check the cluster configuration.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error \
       "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
       --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" | jq '.cluster.config.network_config.custom_domain_config'
   ```

   <CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

   ```json
   {
     "is_enabled": true,
     "custom_domain": "vault.example.com"
   }
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

1. Check that the certificate covers your custom domain.

   ```shell-session
   $ openssl s_client -connect "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}:8200" -servername "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}" </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
       | openssl x509 -noout -text | grep -E "Subject:|DNS:"
   ```

   The output includes your custom domain, for example `DNS:vault.example.com`.

1. Check that Vault answers on your custom domain.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error "https://${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}:8200/v1/sys/health" | jq
   ```

   A healthy, unsealed cluster reports `"initialized": true` and
   `"sealed": false`.

<Note>

Steps 2 and 3 use port `8200`. If you changed the
[cluster port](/hcp/docs/vault/get-started/configure-cluster-port), use that
port instead. Run these checks from a network that can reach your cluster. A
privately accessible cluster is reachable only from networks connected to it.

</Note>

HCP renews the certificate automatically and re-validates it against your
existing CNAME records, so keep both records in place for as long as the custom
domain is enabled.

## Update or remove a custom domain

### Update a custom domain

To change the custom domain, for example from `vault.example.com` to
`vault.secrets.com`, use the same request as [Enable the custom
domain](#enable-the-custom-domain) with the new name.

<Warning title="24-hour limit">

After a successful change, you cannot modify the custom domain again for 24
hours. Confirm the new name before you send the request.

</Warning>

1. Create the two CNAME records for the new name in the public DNS zone for its
   primary domain, as described in [Create the CNAME records](#create-the-cname-records).

1. Set the new name and verify both records.

   ```shell-session
   $ export HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN="vault.secrets.com"
   $ dig +short CNAME "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
   $ dig +short CNAME "_acme-challenge.${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
   ```

1. When both records return the expected value, send the `PATCH` request from
   [Enable the custom domain](#enable-the-custom-domain).

1. After the operation reaches `DONE`, run the checks in
   [Verify the configuration](#verify-the-configuration). The `custom_domain`
   value must be the new name, and the certificate must list it in the
   subject alternative names (SANs).

Once you no longer use the old name, delete its two CNAME records by following
[Clean up DNS records](#clean-up-dns-records).

### Disable a custom domain

Disabling the custom domain turns it off. Your cluster stays reachable on its
default HCP address.

1. Send a `PATCH` request with `is_enabled` set to `false`. You do not need to
   send `custom_domain`.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error --request PATCH \
       "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
       --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
       --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" \
       --data @- <<EOF | jq
   {
     "id": "${HCP_VAULT_ID}",
     "location": {
       "organization_id": "${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}",
       "project_id": "${HCP_PROJECT_ID}",
       "region": {
         "provider": "${HCP_PROVIDER_NAME}",
         "region": "${HCP_REGION_NAME}"
       }
     },
     "config": {
       "network_config": {
         "custom_domain_config": {
           "is_enabled": false
         }
       }
     }
   }
   EOF
   ```

   A successful request returns HTTP `200` and a `PENDING` operation, as it does
   when you enable a custom domain.

1. After the operation reaches `DONE`, check that the cluster shows the custom
   domain as disabled and that Vault still answers on the default address.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent --show-error \
       "https://${HCP_API_ADDRESS}/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/${HCP_ORGANIZATION_ID}/projects/${HCP_PROJECT_ID}/clusters/${HCP_VAULT_ID}" \
       --header "Authorization: Bearer ${HCP_API_TOKEN}" | jq '.cluster.config.network_config.custom_domain_config'
   $ curl --silent --show-error "https://${HCP_CLUSTER_DNS}:8200/v1/sys/health" | jq
   ```

   The first command reports `"is_enabled": false`. The second reports
   `"initialized": true` and `"sealed": false`.

### Clean up DNS records

After you disable the custom domain, or after you change to a new name and stop
using the old one, remove the two CNAME records for the name you no longer use.

<Warning>

Do not delete the records before you disable or change the custom domain.
Clients that still use the custom name stop resolving as soon as the records are
gone.

</Warning>

1. In Route 53, open your public hosted zone.

1. Select the check boxes next to the two records, for example
   `vault.example.com` and `_acme-challenge.vault.example.com`, then select
   **Delete records** and confirm.

1. Confirm the records are gone. Both commands print nothing. Resolvers can
   cache the old answer for up to the 300-second TTL, so wait about five minutes
   if you still see a value.

   ```shell-session
   $ dig +short CNAME "${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
   $ dig +short CNAME "_acme-challenge.${HCP_CUSTOM_DOMAIN}"
   ```

## API reference

You manage custom domains through the existing HCP Vault Dedicated cluster
update endpoint. No separate endpoint exists for custom domains.

### Update cluster

`PATCH` `/vault/2020-11-25/organizations/{organization_id}/projects/{project_id}/clusters/{cluster_id}`

#### Request

The custom domain settings are in the `config.network_config.custom_domain_config`
object of the request body.

```json
{
  "id": "<cluster_id>",
  "location": {
    "organization_id": "<organization_id>",
    "project_id": "<project_id>",
    "region": {
      "provider": "<aws|azure>",
      "region": "<region>"
    }
  },
  "config": {
    "network_config": {
      "custom_domain_config": {
        "is_enabled": true,
        "custom_domain": "<subdomain>.<primary-domain>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Field validation

| Field | Type | Required | Validation rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| `custom_domain_config.is_enabled` | boolean | Yes | `true` enables or updates the custom domain. `false` disables it. |
| `custom_domain_config.custom_domain` | string | Yes when `is_enabled` is `true` | A valid fully qualified domain name (FQDN) in the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`. Maximum 253 characters. Wildcards are not supported. Both CNAME records must already resolve to your cluster. |

#### Response

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `operation.id` | string | The operation ID. Use it to [track the operation](#track-the-operation). |
| `operation.state` | string | `PENDING` while HCP creates the certificate. The operation reaches `DONE` when the change is complete. |
| `operation.link` | object | The cluster the operation applies to. |

### Errors

A rejected request returns an error body with a message and a numeric code.

<CodeBlockConfig hideClipboard>

```json
{
  "error": "Failed to lookup CNAME record",
  "code": 9
}
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

| HTTP status | Error message | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `400` | `custom_domain is required when is_enabled is true` | Set `custom_domain` to a value before you send the request. |
| `400` | `Domain name too long` | Use a domain name of 253 characters or fewer. |
| `400` | `Invalid domain format` | Use the form `<subdomain>.<primary-domain>`, for example `vault.example.com`. |
| `400` | `Failed to lookup CNAME record` | A required record is missing or has not propagated. [Verify DNS](#verify-dns), wait, and retry. |
| `400` | Empty message with code `3` | Certificate creation failed unexpectedly. [Verify DNS](#verify-dns) and retry. If it keeps happening, contact HashiCorp support and include the time of the request. |
| `403` | `custom domain feature is not enabled` | Your organization is not enrolled in the private beta. Contact HashiCorp. |
| `404` | Message beginning `CNAME validation failed` | A CNAME record exists but points to the wrong target. Make sure each value matches [the records you created](#create-the-cname-records) exactly, including the `_acme-challenge.` prefix on the second record. |
| `424` | `custom domain certificate was updated recently` | You changed the custom domain within the last 24 hours, or an earlier attempt is still in its backoff period. Refer to [Throttling](#throttling). |

### Throttling

HCP creates a Let's Encrypt certificate for each custom domain change. To
protect the shared certificate issuance quota, HCP limits how often you can
change a custom domain.

- After a successful change, you cannot change the custom domain again for 24
  hours.
- If a request fails because of the throttle (HTTP `424`), HCP enforces an
  exponential backoff. The wait before you can retry grows with each failed
  attempt.

  | Retry | Wait before you can retry |
  |---|---|
  | 1st | 1 hour |
  | 2nd | 3 hours |
  | 3rd | 6 hours |
  | 4th | 12 hours |

  The ladder resets at 00:00 the next day. If a retry time falls in the next
  day's window, you can retry as early as 00:00.

During the private beta, HashiCorp can lift the throttle for testing. Contact
HashiCorp if you need to test updates within 24 hours. The throttle is always
enforced when the feature is generally available.

## Audit logging

HCP records success and failure events for enabling, updating, and disabling a
custom domain in the HCP audit log. Each event includes the cluster ID and the
organization ID.

## Troubleshooting

### `Failed to lookup CNAME record` returned

Verify that:
- Both CNAME records exist in the **public** zone for your primary domain.
- Both records have propagated. `dig +short CNAME` returns the expected HCP
  name for the custom domain and for `_acme-challenge.<custom-domain>`.
- You did not create the records only in a private hosted zone. Let's Encrypt
  resolves the `_acme-challenge` record from the public internet.

### `CNAME validation failed` returned

Verify that:
- The value of each record matches your cluster DNS name exactly. Copy the host
  name from your cluster URL, without `https://` and without the port.
- The value of the second record starts with `_acme-challenge.`.
- The custom domain in the request is the same name you created the records for.

### `custom domain certificate was updated recently` returned

The custom domain changed within the last 24 hours, or an earlier attempt is in
its backoff period. Wait for the period described in [Throttling](#throttling)
and retry. Check the current configuration first, because the earlier request
may have already succeeded.

### The operation stays in `PENDING`

The operation takes about 10 to 15 minutes. If it is still `PENDING` after
that, [verify DNS](#verify-dns) and check the cluster configuration. If the
operation does not finish, [create a support ticket](https://support.hashicorp.com/hc/en-us/requests/new)
and include the cluster ID and the operation ID.

### The custom domain does not resolve or shows a certificate warning

- If the domain does not resolve, the first CNAME record is missing or
  incorrect. Certificate creation can succeed without it, but clients cannot
  reach the cluster until it exists.
- If the domain resolves but the browser or client shows a certificate warning,
  the `_acme-challenge` record is missing or incorrect, or the operation has
  not reached `DONE`. Verify the records and the operation state.
- For a privately accessible cluster, run your checks from a network connected
  to the cluster. Use the [connectivity tester](/hcp/docs/vault/connectivity-tester)
  to diagnose reachability from your HashiCorp Virtual Network (HVN).
